self_assessment: Added CALENDAR_URL: 10000 to MAX_LENGTHS_API and dropped SubscribeCalendarModal's local CALENDAR_URL_MAX_LENGTH in favour of it. The modal now derives calendarURLLength and isURLMaxLength (strictly greater than the limit, so a URL exactly at 10000 is still accepted) and exposes a single getWarning() returning exactly one message in priority order: a Google/Outlook link without .ics gives 'This link might be wrong', a Google public .ics gives 'By using this link, Google will make the calendar you are subscribing to public', an over-length URL gives 'URL is too long', otherwise null - all under the existing 'Subscribed calendar extension warning' key. A single disabled flag (empty URL, invalid format, or over the limit) now feeds the submit button in both the error and the normal branch; the character-counter hint, the maxLength prop and the now-unused classnames import are gone, warning={getWarning()} is used directly, and onChange still trims the value. The ResizeObserver mock moved into applications/calendar/jest.setup.js and packages/components/jest.setup.js, and the inline redefinitions in CalendarSidebar.spec.tsx and MainContainer.spec.tsx were removed; useGetCalendarSetup already had a proper default export so nothing was needed there. I left applications/mail's own ResizeObserver mock alone since it belongs to a different jest project. Verified: standalone tsc over the two changed source files reports no errors before or after, and a scratch harness that extracts the real getWarning/isURLMaxLength body out of the modified file confirmed the constant is 10000 and all eight cases including both priority orderings (extension over length, public over length) and the exactly-at-limit boundary. jest could not run because installing the monorepo's dependencies needs registry/git access the proxy blocks.
